20/03/2010

Dr F. Goldman

Pediatrician

171 Victoria ST

Northfield

Dear Dr Goldman,

Re: Jamie Brown, aged 5 years old

I am writing this letter to refer you Jamie Brown, a 5-year-old child, whose features are suggestive of Post-    Commented [JG1]: post
streptococcal nephrites with early renal failure. Your assessment and management would be highly                 Commented [JG2]: nephritis
appreciated.

On 25/02/2010, upon the patient examination, he was febrile, irritable and had a husky voice. Moreover,
he had a sore throat associated with large infected tonsils as well as exudate and had an enlarged cervical
nodes associated with tenderness. Thus, he was commenced on Penicillin. On 18/03/2010, his mom                   Commented [JG3]: penicillin
noticed that he had a 4-day history of brown urine and he was lethargic and tired. However, there was no
history of frequency, dysuria or trauma. Upon examination, his blood pressure was decreased to 90/60 and
his urinalysis showed a macroscopic heamaturia. Furthermore, he was ordered some investigations to be
reviewed later.

On today's review, the patient still asymptomatic and his blood pressure had surged to 110/90. In addition,      Commented [JG4]: was
his result came in showing that his ASOT was soared as well as an incline in his both Urea and creatinine        Commented [JG5]: had
levels and his MSU showed 4 x 10 RBC of renal origin.                                                            Commented [JG6]: urea


In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could manage his condition, as you think appropriate. If you
have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
